purpose: Teach: つけ加え/まるまる/たんに/思いのほか/ガタガタ/やっとこ/おのずから/じっさい

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お父さんが「楽しんで」と一言つけ加えて出かけられたわ
lines.en: Sho — your dad added one more thing before he left. He said to enjoy it.
lines.style: Warm observation, stated gently. No urgency. Soft landing on the memory. The tone of someone sharing a small, tender detail.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、お休みをまるまる絵に使ったよ
lines.en: Mom, I used my whole holiday for drawing.
lines.style: Matter-of-fact pride. No boasting — just stating what happened. A small, genuine smile underneath. Direct eye contact with the fact of it.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、たんにお父さんが疲れていらしただけよ
lines.en: Sho, your dad was just tired, that's all.
lines.style: Gentle reframing, not defensive. The tone of a mother explaining something she understands. Quiet certainty, no need to convince.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、お祖父ちゃんに会えて思いのほか嬉しかったよ
lines.en: Mom, I was happier to see Grandpa than I thought I'd be.
lines.style: Small surprise in the voice. Tender discovery — he's noticing his own feeling as he says it. Soft, genuine warmth. No performance.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お家の窓がガタガタ鳴ってるわ
lines.en: Sho, the window at home is rattling.
lines.style: Calm observation, stated as fact. A shift in attention — noticing something practical. Mild concern held steady, not alarmed.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、やっとこ宿題終わったよ
lines.en: Mom, I finally finished my homework.
lines.style: Relief and accomplishment mixed together. Not dramatic — just the quiet satisfaction of something done. A small breath of ease on the word finally.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、おのずから道が開けることもあるのよ
lines.en: Sho, sometimes the path opens up by itself.
lines.style: Philosophical whisper, almost to herself. Patient, accepting tone. The wisdom of someone who has learned this through living. Slow, no rush.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、じっさいお祖父ちゃんに会いたいよ
lines.en: Mom, I really do want to see Grandpa.
lines.style: Direct, earnest need underneath. The word really carries weight — he's being honest, not asking permission. Quiet conviction, a small boy being clear about what matters.
